name: Acesur (Aceites del Sur-Coosur)
desc: Family-based Spanish olive oil and vegetable fats producer founded in 1840, owner of the Coosur and La Española brands.
products: Olive oils and vegetable fats under Coosur, La Española, Guillén, Altivo, Itálica, Oli Nostrum and other brands
customers: Retailers and consumers in Spain and export markets
stores_or_sites: 8 industrial plants (7 in Spain, 1 in Suffolk, Virginia, US)
markets: Spain (Coosur leading olive oil brand) and exports to more than 110-120 countries via La Española; plant in the US

fin.value_orig: EUR 1,364m revenue (latest filed accounts, elEconomista rank 153)

fit_rationale: Family-owned Spanish olive oil house with a consumer export brand (La Española) in 110+ countries; F1 could carry retail promotions and Spanish Grand Prix activation, though B2B hospitality value is modest.
f1_markets: Spain, United States and other export markets
outstanding: Ownership detail (family named), revenue year of the elEconomista figure, sponsorships page not opened.

name: Peter Kittle Motor Company
desc: Family-owned Australian dealership group selling new and used Toyota vehicles through ten dealerships in South Australia, Victoria and NSW.
products: New and used Toyota (and Mazda) vehicles, service and parts
markets: South Australia, Victoria and New South Wales, Australia

fin.value_orig: AUD 529.1m revenue (balance date 6/22; IBISWorld Top 500 Private 2022 rank 126; older than 3 years)

fit_rationale: Regional Toyota franchise dealer with no brand of its own beyond Australian local markets; F1 offers little it needs, and Toyota-linked F1 activity limits category freedom.
category_conflict: potential: Toyota (Haas title partner) is the brand it retails
outstanding: Revenue is FY2022 (older than 3 years); HQ city not stated; employees.

name: Charter Schools USA
desc: Family-owned US education management company founded in 1997 that operates 154 charter schools across four south-eastern states.
customers: Charter school boards and public school authorities; students and families
markets: Florida, Louisiana, North Carolina and South Carolina, United States

alt_indicators.evidence: Clay modelled revenue bracket USD 1B-10B (estimate, not reported)

fit_rationale: US school operator funded through public charter contracts; Miami and Austin races aside, F1 has little commercial role for a domestic education manager with no consumer product to sell.

access.roles: Founder and CEO; chief marketing/communications officer

outstanding: Ownership structure beyond 'family-owned'; reported revenue; number of states (4 vs 5).

name: KDS Group
desc: Private Bangladeshi conglomerate making garments, textiles, trims and packaging and steel, with logistics, shipping and property businesses.
products: Garments, textiles, accessories and packaging, steel (KDS Steel, KYCR Coil), logistics, property
customers: International apparel brands and Bangladeshi industrial buyers
markets: Bangladesh (Chittagong and Dhaka); garments exported to international buyers
fit_rationale: Chittagong garments and steel group selling B2B to apparel buyers; no consumer brand and no Grand Prix in its home market, so F1 value would be limited to buyer hospitality.

access.roles: Chairman; managing director; group marketing head

outstanding: Current revenue (2012 figure only); whether KDS Accessories is listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (the group holding is stated private); website.

name: SEB (Grupo SEB / SEB Education)
desc: Brazilian-origin private school group running about 505 schools for 78,000 students in Brazil and more than 35 countries.
products: Private K-12 schools and education services
markets: Brazil plus schools in 35-38 countries worldwide

alt_indicators.evidence: listed among the biggest players in the international private school market (141 schools at the time)

fit_rationale: International private-school operator with consumer-facing school brands in Brazil and abroad; São Paulo and other Grand Prix cities match some markets, but parents are an indirect F1 audience.
f1_markets: Brazil and other GP countries among its 35+ markets
outstanding: Ownership (founder named nowhere on pages opened), HQ city, revenue, employees, the school brands it runs.

name: Kreissparkasse Köln
desc: German public-law savings bank owned by four Rhineland districts, with EUR 31bn total assets and 143 business locations around Cologne.
products: Retail and business banking, lending, deposits, securities
customers: Private and business customers in the Cologne region
parent_immediate: Zweckverband of Rhein-Erft-Kreis, Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis and Oberbergischer Kreis
marketing_autonomy_basis: independent savings bank under municipal ownership
markets: Cologne region districts of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany

fin.value_orig: total assets EUR 31.113bn (2025) - balance-sheet total, not revenue or AUM

fit_rationale: Regional savings bank bound to its four Rhineland districts with EUR 4m local community giving; no Grand Prix in Germany and a regional mandate make F1 a poor fit.

access.roles: Management board chair; head of marketing and communications

outstanding: Total assets recorded in fin as balance-sheet figure (no route metric); revenue/income figures not opened.

name: Clementoni
desc: Italian private toy and puzzle maker from Recanati, led by the founding Clementoni family, with EUR 210m revenue.
marketing_autonomy_basis: private company led by founder's son Giovanni Clementoni
markets: Italy (HQ); international distribution not detailed on pages opened
fit_rationale: Family-run Italian puzzle and toy brand; an F1 licence could drive licensed puzzles and science kits and an Imola/Monza retail push, with no current F1 partner in its category.
outstanding: Share ownership (page names family managers, not shareholders) and whether it remains independent; international subsidiaries; newer revenue.

name: Tragsa (Empresa de Transformación Agraria)
aliases: Empresa De Transformacion Agraria Sa Sme Mp
subsector: public rural, environmental and infrastructure works
desc: Spanish state-owned group delivering rural development, environmental, water and infrastructure works and emergency services for public administrations.
products: Rural development, nature conservation, infrastructure works, water, food safety and animal health, IT and consulting, emergencies
customers: Spanish central, regional and local administrations
marketing_autonomy_basis: in-house public service provider of the Spanish state
markets: Spain, plus 125 Spanish cooperation projects in Africa, Latin America, Asia, Europe and the Middle East

fin.value_orig: EUR 1,350m revenue (latest filed accounts, elEconomista rank 156)

fit_rationale: State in-house provider working only for Spanish administrations; it wins work by public commission, not marketing, so F1 sponsorship has almost no commercial purpose.

name: CFAO
subsector: vehicle and consumer distribution in Africa
desc: Toyota Tsusho-owned distributor of vehicles, equipment, pharmaceuticals, consumer goods and retail across 38 African countries and French overseas territories.
products: Automotive distribution (Toyota, Suzuki, Hino), equipment, fleet leasing (LOXEA), pharmaceuticals, consumer goods, shopping centres, IT and energy
customers: Businesses, governments, NGOs and consumers in Africa
markets: 38 African countries (91% of sales) and 6 French overseas departments and collectivities
fit_rationale: Africa-focused Toyota and Suzuki distributor and retailer; F1 could support dealer and government-client hospitality, but no Grand Prix in Africa and Toyota already sits in F1 via Haas.
category_conflict: potential: Toyota (Haas title partner) is its main distributed brand and its parent's group

access.roles: CEO; group communications director; division heads

outstanding: Own website not opened; marketing autonomy from Toyota Tsusho.

name: Bing Lee
desc: Family-run Australian electrical and appliance retailer, the largest privately held one in New South Wales, with about 31 stores.
products: Consumer electronics, home appliances, specialist appliance showrooms
customers: Consumers in New South Wales and the ACT
marketing_autonomy_basis: fourth-generation family business, CEO Lionel Lee

fin.value_orig: AUD 524.0m revenue (balance date 6/22; IBISWorld Top 500 Private 2022 rank 130; older than 3 years)

fit_rationale: NSW electronics retailer that already buys Sydney football sponsorship; F1 broadcast promotions could fit its TV sales, but its single-state footprint makes a global championship poor value.
outstanding: Revenue is FY2022 (older than 3 years); employees; current status of sponsorships.
